tool_input.prompt: List the current minor release for each major version (esp. 16 and the latest major), end-of-life dates, and any 'last updated' date on the page.

tool_result_content:
**Current minor releases and end-of-life dates**

| Version | Current minor | Supported | First release | Final release (EOL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **18** (latest in the table) | **18.6** | Yes | Sep 25, 2025 | Nov 14, 2030 |
| **17** | 17.11 | Yes | Sep 26, 2024 | Nov 8, 2029 |
| **16** | **16.15** | Yes | Sep 14, 2023 | Nov 9, 2028 |
| **15** | 15.19 | Yes | Oct 13, 2022 | Nov 11, 2027 |
| **14** | 14.24 | Yes | Sep 30, 2021 | Nov 12, 2026 |
| 13 | 13.23 | No | Sep 24, 2020 | Nov 13, 2025 |
| 12 | 12.22 | No | Oct 3, 2019 | Nov 21, 2024 |
| 11 | 11.22 | No | Oct 18, 2018 | Nov 9, 2023 |
| 10 | 10.23 | No | Oct 5, 2017 | Nov 10, 2022 |
| 9.6 | 9.6.24 | No | Sep 29, 2016 | Nov 11, 2021 |

Versions 9.5 and older are also end-of-life. The last one, 6.3, ended support on March 1, 2003.

**Notes**

- **PostgreSQL 16:** Current minor is 16.15. It is supported until November 9, 2028.
- **Latest major in the table:** PostgreSQL 18, current minor 18.6, supported until November 14, 2030. The page's news banner also announces **PostgreSQL 19 RC 1** (October 15, 2026), but 19 is not yet in the table.
- **Upcoming EOL:** PostgreSQL 14 reaches end-of-life on November 12, 2026.
- **Last updated date:** The page does not show one. The most recent dates are the October 15, 2026 news item and the copyright line "1996-2026."
